work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI (presentation/web_ui.py and helpers). You should make update to css in web_ui.py directly. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests for the web_ui.py to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via the web UI.
The CSS updates in web_ui.py correctly apply styles for both themes.
Query syntax highlighting and result panels remain readable in both themes.
User’s theme preference is saved in local storage and persists across page reloads.
Unit tests cover the theme toggle functionality and CSS application.

analysis.summary: Implement a toggleable dark/light theme within the existing Python-rendered web UI by updating CSS directly in web_ui.py, ensuring syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, and persisting user preference using local storage.
technical_requirements: Add light/dark theme selection functionality within presentation/web_ui.py and helpers.
Update CSS styles directly in web_ui.py to support both themes.
Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels are legible in both themes.
Persist user’s theme choice across requests using browser local storage.
Add unit tests in web_ui.py to verify dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via the web UI.
The CSS updates in web_ui.py correctly apply styles for both themes.
Query syntax highlighting and result panels remain readable in both themes.
User’s theme preference is saved in local storage and persists across page reloads.
Unit tests cover the theme toggle functionality and CSS application.
risks: Direct CSS updates in Python code may be error-prone and harder to maintain.
Ensuring all UI elements, especially syntax highlighting and result panels, remain legible under both themes.
Cross-browser compatibility and local storage availability.
Potential UI flicker or delay when applying persisted theme on page load.
analysis.recommended_approach: Modify web_ui.py to include CSS definitions for both dark and light themes and implement a toggle control in the UI. Use JavaScript embedded or injected via Python to handle theme switching and store the preference in local storage. On page load, read the stored preference and apply the corresponding theme CSS. Add unit tests to verify theme toggling logic and CSS application.

implementation_steps.description: Add CSS styles for both dark and light themes directly in presentation/web_ui.py, including styles for query syntax highlighting and result panels to ensure legibility.

instructions: Define CSS styles for light and dark themes as string constants or variables.
Include CSS rules for syntax highlighting and result panels for both themes.
Add a CSS class or data attribute to the root HTML element to switch themes.

implementation_steps.validation: Verify that CSS styles for both themes are present in the web_ui.py and cover all relevant UI elements.

implementation_steps.description: Implement a theme toggle control in the UI rendered by web_ui.py and embed JavaScript to handle theme switching and persist the user's choice in local storage.

instructions: Add a toggle button or switch in the HTML output to allow users to switch between dark and light themes.
Embed JavaScript that listens for toggle events, applies the selected theme by modifying the root element's class or attribute, and saves the preference to local storage.
On page load, read the stored theme preference from local storage and apply the corresponding theme automatically.

implementation_steps.validation: Test in a browser that toggling the theme updates the UI immediately and that the selected theme persists after page reload.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented toggleable dark/light theme support in the Python-rendered web UI (presentation/web_ui.py). Added CSS styles for both themes directly in web_ui.py, including syntax highlighting and result panel styles to ensure legibility. Introduced a UI toggle control with embedded JavaScript to switch themes and persist user preference in local storage. Added unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and CSS application. This enhancement improves user experience by allowing seamless switching between dark and light modes with preference persistence across page reloads.
